nodes.title: Keystroke Dynamics: Concepts, Techniques, and Applications
nodes.dataset: Includes novel keystroke datasets, touch screen/mobile device data, and benchmarking resources. Covers free-text, fixed-text, and semi-fixed-text keystroke data.
nodes.methodology: A comprehensive survey of recent developments in keystroke dynamics research (2013–present), including datasets, algorithms, and applications. Articles were categorized by contributions to datasets, algorithms, feature engineering, mobile device integration, and applications.
nodes.contribution: Provides a holistic review of keystroke dynamics, including datasets, algorithms, feature engineering, mobile device applications, and future research directions. Highlights gaps in prior surveys.

nodes.title: Identifying Users’ Emotional States through Keystroke Dynamics
nodes.dataset: EmoSurv dataset with 124 subjects, containing keystroke data and emotion labels (Anger, Happiness, Calmness, Sadness, Neutral State) collected via fixed/free text typing tasks and emotion-inducing videos.
nodes.methodology: A time-windowing approach analyzes writing sessions in batches, enabling emotion recognition from short typing windows (e.g., 30 seconds) using features derived from dwell time, flight time, and key press patterns.
nodes.contribution: Introduces time-windowing for KD-based emotion recognition and demonstrates its viability for social media applications with fast typing rhythms.

nodes.title: Estimation of the User’s Emotional State by Keystroke Dynamics
nodes.dataset: Fixed text from 'Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland' and free text input with periodic keystroke monitoring.
nodes.methodology: Analyzes keystroke dynamics (timing and frequency parameters) to infer emotional states via fixed/free text input and user self-reports.
nodes.contribution: Introduces keystroke dynamics as a non-intrusive, cost-effective method for emotion recognition in real-world applications.

nodes.title: AN IMPROVED MODEL FOR EMOTION-AWARE COMPUTING DEVICES USING KEYSTROKE DYNAMICS AND SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE
nodes.dataset: Participants' keystrokes and self-reported emotional states from a field study.
nodes.methodology: Keystroke dynamics analysis combined with SVM to create models for six emotional states. Field study collected keystroke data and self-reported emotional states for training.
nodes.contribution: Proposed an emotion-aware model using keystroke dynamics and SVM, providing recommendations for future research and data collection.

nodes.title: The influence of emotion on keyboard typing: an experimental study using visual stimuli
nodes.dataset: Keystroke data from 27 subjects under different emotional states induced by IAPS stimuli.
nodes.methodology: Controlled experiment with IAPS-induced emotional states. Two-way Valence (3) × Arousal (3) ANOVAs analyzed keystroke data.
nodes.contribution: Supports that keystroke duration, latency, and accuracy are influenced by emotions. Suggests personalized models could enhance emotion recognition.
